why_ai: Unlicensed SaaS whose core reading and drafting work AI-native contract tools now perform directly.
why_clarity: Implementations fail often because value depends on each customer's messy back catalogue and configuration.
why_digital: Contracts in, software and structured data out, sold remotely to enterprises.

why_ai: Extraction from a static PDF corpus is exactly what current language models already do adequately.
why_clarity: Thousands of executed agreements yield defined obligation fields checkable against the source text.
why_digital: PDF agreements in, structured obligation data out, entirely on screens.

why_ai: Standard order forms and NDAs self-served from templates need no lawyer and no judgment.
why_clarity: Requesters need a standard contract or a status, delivered the same way thousands of times.
why_digital: Request forms in, generated contracts and status updates out online.

why_ai: Comparing executed agreements with the library is automatable, though acceptable positions need senior judgment.
why_clarity: Drift is detectable from executed text, but what the library should say is a lawyer's call.
why_digital: Executed contracts and clause text compared and curated entirely in software.

why_ai: In-house counsel negotiate adversarially against counterparties and answer for the terms they accept.
why_clarity: Achievable positions depend on counterparty and leverage; whether terms were good emerges much later.
why_digital: Redlines exchanged as documents and calls, with tools bought remotely by legal teams.

why_ai: Applying known positions to recognised provisions is mechanical work current models already perform.
why_clarity: Routine edits apply a written playbook position to recurring provisions, checkable by counsel.
why_digital: Contract documents in, tracked-change redlines out on screen.

why_ai: Routing incoming agreements by risk signals present in the document is a classification task for software.
why_clarity: Every request gets a risk tier and route, though misroutes surface only after review.
why_digital: Requests and attached documents in, routing decisions out, all within software queues.

why_ai: Buyers with nobody to configure tools want automatic value, which favours AI-native self-serve software.
why_clarity: Small-company contract needs repeat, but success is vague without legal operations to define it.
why_digital: Contracts from shared drives processed by software bought online by office managers.

why_ai: A cross-company terms corpus is hard to replicate, but no licence or personal relationship protects it.
why_clarity: Achievability is probabilistic by counterparty and deal size, confirmed only when negotiations close.
why_digital: Pooled contract data analysed and delivered as benchmarks through software.

why_ai: Joining contract terms to operational system data is a data-integration task software performs.
why_clarity: A service level is met or missed, checkable against operational data each period.
why_digital: Contract terms and operational metrics joined and alerted on entirely in software.

why_ai: Counsel signs off on counterparty paper, but absence detection against a standard is tractable for AI.
why_clarity: Missing protective terms reveal themselves only when a dispute arises years later.
why_digital: Counterparty documents in, review memos and redlines out, entirely on screens.
